claim: A comparison of Sarkozy's 2007/2012 presidential vote maps versus Le Pen's/RN's more recent maps shows that the sociological transfer of the traditional right electorate to RN was not an exact transfer of electoral geography — RN's map has shifted, not stayed fixed.
stance_target: assumption that a party's electoral geography is stable/transferable across time and election types
scope_conditions: France, presidential 2007/2012 vs. legislative 2024, departmental scale
quoted_support: Une comparaison suivie des cartes du vote Sarkozy en 2007 et 2012 par rapport au vote Le Pen montre toutefois que ce transfert électoral n'est pas exactement un transfert de la géographie électorale.

claim: In the 2024 legislative first round, RN achieved its largest gains relative to 2017 outside its historical strongholds, notably in the traditionally left-leaning Southwest: +18.1 points in Tarn-et-Garonne, +17.9 in Lot-et-Garonne, +16.8 in Dordogne.
stance_target: stability of RN's geographic base as a fixed predictor
scope_conditions: France, legislative first round 2017 vs 2024, departmental scale, Southwest France
quoted_support: dans le Sud-Ouest, longtemps considéré comme un bastion de la gauche, il connaît une forte croissance par rapport à 2017 : +18,1 points dans le Tarn-et-Garonne, +17,9 dans le Lot-et-Garonne, +16,8 en Dordogne.

claim: RN's historical strongholds intensified sharply between 2017 and 2024 even as the base expanded elsewhere: Haute-Marne rose from 17% (2007 FN level, 2nd department nationally) to 50.8% RN in 2024; Pas-de-Calais reached 48.7%, and Var 49.6%.
stance_target: intensity trajectory of RN strongholds across 2007-2024
quoted_support: La Haute-Marne affichait 17 % de vote RN (contre 50,8 % en 2024) et était le 2e département à voter RN, derrière l'Aisne.

claim: RN's electorate has evolved from an initially homogeneous base toward a diversified coalition increasingly resembling the electorate that supported Sarkozy in 2007 and 2012, per political scientist Jean-Yves Dormagen.
stance_target: sociological transformation of RN electorate as driver of geographic expansion
quoted_support: la conquête du RN part d'un électorat au départ assez homogène vers un électorat aujourd'hui très diversifié — qui ressemble de plus en plus à la coalition électorale ayant porté ses suffrages sur Nicolas Sarkozy en 2007 et 2012.
